name: Balanced 4-4-2

slots.why: Rolls the ball to full-backs when they are available or kicks longer toward the flanks to bypass central pressure; no sweeping needed in a flat block.
Support full-back gives width behind the winger and covers when the winger goes forward.

Central defender in a flat pair. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the keeper kicks long to the flanks and the pair is not asked to build. Only one centre-back may use Cover.

Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the keeper kicks long to the flanks and the pair is not asked to build. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Winger (Support) provides width and crosses for the two strikers.
Defensive central midfielder screens the defence and does the simple work.
Supporting central midfielder links the wingers and strikers with the defensive midfielder.
Winger (Support) on the right, giving the same width and crossing.
Deep-lying forward (or Complete Forward) holds the ball and links with the other striker.
Advanced Forward runs in behind the defence; Poacher is the alternate for a striker who finishes better than he runs.

description: A simple two-banks-of-four structure with natural width and two complementary forwards.
whyGood: It is easy to recruit for, tactically clear and gives a useful baseline against more specialised systems.
whyThisShape: Two flat banks of four with two strikers, the most familiar shape in the game. It is easy to understand, gives every player a clear job, and puts two strikers against two centre-backs. Fairly wide attacking width lets the wingers and full-backs stretch the opponent, while slightly more direct passing reaches the forwards without demanding intricate midfield combinations. Standard tempo, balanced focus and no forced passes into space keep it a steady baseline rather than an all-out vertical attack. Mixed crossing and disciplined play are starting fallbacks to review against the selected players. The goalkeeper can roll to available full-backs or kick longer toward the flanks, with no fixed instruction to rush or slow distribution. Standard pressing and lines preserve the two banks without forcing tighter marking or a press on short goalkeeper distribution. It is thin in central midfield against a three.
whenToUse: As a solid default, or when you have two good strikers and two decent wingers. It is also the shape most lower-league squads can fill without a specialist.
whenNotToUse: Against a team with three central midfielders who will pass through the middle, since your two are outnumbered.

instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Be More Disciplined: Ask players to retain the defined structure rather than adding further improvisation.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Reach the forward outlets earlier without turning every possession into a long ball.
instructionRationale.Sometimes Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

keyRequirements: Two complementary strikers, with one linking and one attacking space
Wingers with enough crossing to supply the front two
A disciplined central midfielder paired with a reliable support midfielder
Full-backs able to support without being the main attacking outlet
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
